([[Rancho Cucamonga, California]]) | college = [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] (2014–2018) | draft_year = 2018 | career_start = 2018 | years1 = [[2018–19 NBA G League season|2018–2019]] | team1 = [[Long Island Nets]] | years2 = {{nbay|2019|start}}–{{nbay|2023|end}} | team2 = [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] | years3 = [[2019–20 NBA G League season|2019–2020]] | team3 = →[[Iowa Wolves]] | years4 = {{nbay|2024|start}}–{{nbay|2024|end}} | team4 = [[Sacramento Kings]] | years5 = {{nbay|2024|end}}–present | team5 = [[San Antonio Spurs]] | highlights = *First-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] ([[2017–18 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|2018]]) }} '''Jordan McLaughlin''' (born April 9, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[San Antonio Spurs]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC Trojans]]. ==High school career== McLaughlin is the son of Thomas McLaughlin, who played minor league baseball, and has an older sister, Amber. Growing up, Jordan played baseball and football but gravitated towards basketball.{{cite news |last1=Kaufman |first1=Joey |title=How Jordan McLaughlin led USC's basketball revival |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2018/03/02/how-jordan-mclaughlin-led-uscs-basketball-revival/ |access-date=July 8, 2018 |work=[[Orange County Register]] |date=March 2, 2018}} McLaughlin attended [[Etiwanda High School]] in [[Rancho Cucamonga, California]]. He scored 19 points in the 2013 Chicago Elite Classic.{{cite web|url=http://articles.latimes.com/2013/dec/07/sports/la-sp-vi-boys-basketball-etiwanda-wins-in-chicago-to-improve-to-50-20131207|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222205604/http://articles.latimes.com/2013/dec/07/sports/la-sp-vi-boys-basketball-etiwanda-wins-in-chicago-to-improve-to-50-20131207|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 22, 2014|title=Boys' basketball: Etiwanda wins in Chicago to improve to 5-0 [Updated]|access-date=January 31, 2014|date=December 7, 2013|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|author=Sondheimer, Eric}} He committed to the USC Trojans over scholarship offers from [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]]. USC coach [[Andy Enfield]] made him a recruiting priority after seeing him at an AAU game.{{cite news |last1=Lindsey |first1=Thiry |title=Jordan McLaughlin turned out to be the perfect fit for Andy Enfield and USC basketball |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/usc/la-sp-usc-jordan-mclaughlin-20180301-story.html# |access-date=July 8, 2018 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=March 1, 2018}} McLaughlin had previously crossed USC off his list after seeing former coach [[Kevin O'Neill (basketball)|Kevin O'Neill]] berate an injured player at a practice. ==College career== [[File:Jordan McLaughlin USC.jpg|thumb|left|McLaughlin with the USC Trojans in 2016]] In his freshman season, USC won 12 games. He averaged 12.1 points and 4.5 assists per game but missed the end of the season with a shoulder injury.{{cite news |last1=Jorgensen |first1=Jack |title=USC's Jordan McLaughlin (shoulder) out for season |url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/02/26/jordan-mclaughlin-usc-shoulder-injury-out-season |access-date=July 8, 2018 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=February 26, 2015}} McLaughlin led USC to the NCAA Tournament in 2016, and averaged 13.4 points per game on 47 percent shooting.{{cite news |last1=Kaufman |first1=Joey |title=USC point guard Jordan McLaughlin strong to the finish |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2016/12/16/usc-point-guard-jordan-mclaughlin-strong-to-the-finish/ |access-date=July 8, 2018 |work=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |date=December 16, 2016}} He led the team back to the NCAA tournament in 2017, posting 12.9 points, 3.6 rebounds and 5.5 assists per game. Coming into his senior year, he was named to the preseason [[Bob Cousy Award]] Watchlist.{{cite news |last1=Pederson |first1=Brian |title=USC standouts Jordan McLaughlin, De'Anthony Melton named to preseason watch lists |url=https://www.myajc.com/sports/college/usc-standouts-jordan-mclaughlin-anthony-melton-named-preseason-watch-lists/5OKLjdy4i3G2ldsdKmlNoI/ |access-date=July 8, 2018 |work=[[Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |date=October 17, 2017}} As a senior at USC, McLaughlin averaged 12.8 points, 7.8 assists, 3.7 rebounds and 2.0 steals in 35.3 minutes per game, shooting 39.7 percent from behind the arc.{{cite news |title=Nets' Jordan McLaughlin: Will play summer league with Nets |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/nets-jordan-mclaughlin-will-play-summer-league-with-nets/ |access-date=July 8, 2018 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=June 27, 2018}} He was a First Team All-Pac-12 selection.{{Cite web|url=http://pac-12.com/article/2018/03/04/2017-18-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-teams-announced|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180306044202/http://pac-12.com/article/2018/03/04/2017-18-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-teams-announced|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 6, 2018|title=2017-18 Pac-12 Men's Basketball All-Conference Teams announced|website=[[Pac-12 Conference]]|access-date=July 8, 2018}} McLaughlin was named to the All-District IX Team by the USBWA and First Team All-District 20 by the NABC.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2018/alldistrict180306.html|title=USBWA NAMES 2017-18 MEN'S ALL-DISTRICT TEAMS|website=sportswriters.net|date=March 6, 2018|access-date=March 6, 2018}}{{cite press release|title=National Association of Basketball Coaches Announces 2017-18 Division I All-District Teams|date=March 13, 2018|publisher=National Association of Basketball Coaches|url=http://www.nabc.com/awards/all_district/2017-18_NABC_Division_I_ALL-DISTRICT_TEAMS.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180315220821/http://www.nabc.com/awards/all_district/2017-18_NABC_Division_I_ALL-DISTRICT_TEAMS.pdf|archive-date=March 15, 2018|url-status=live}} His assists per game was the third highest in Division I, and McLaughlin was the third Pac-12 player ever to record more than 600 assists and 1,600 points over a career.{{cite news |last1=Kaufmann |first1=Joey |title=Undrafted USC guards Elijah Stewart, Jordan McLaughlin to join NBA summer league teams |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2018/06/22/undrafted-usc-guards-elijah-stewart-jordan-mclaughlin-to-join-nba-summer-league-teams/ |access-date=July 8, 2018 |work=[[Orange County Register]] |date=June 22, 2018}} ==Professional career== ===Long Island Nets (2018–2019)=== After going undrafted in the [[2018 NBA draft]], McLaughlin signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]] for NBA summer league play. He was also invited to training camp. He scored seven points and six assists in 90–76 summer league loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] on July 7.{{cite news |title=Nets' Jordan McLaughlin: Hands out six assists |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/nets-jordan-mclaughlin-hands-out-six-assists/ |access-date=July 8, 2018 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=July 7, 2018}} McLaughlin later joined the Nets on a training camp deal.{{cite web |title=BROOKLYN NETS SIGN MITCHELL CREEK AND JORDAN MCLAUGHLIN |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2018/08/20/brooklyn-nets-sign-mitchell-creek-and-jordan-mclaughlin |website=NBA.com |access-date=August 20, 2018 |date=August 20, 2018}} He was waived by the Nets on October 11,{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Waive McLaughlin And Omot |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2018/10/11/brooklyn-nets-waive-mclaughlin-and-omot |website=NBA.com |access-date=October 11, 2018 |date=October 11, 2018}} but was signed to the training camp roster of the Nets’ [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Long Island Nets]].{{cite web|title=Long Island Nets Finalize Training Camp Roster|url=https://longisland.gleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-finalize-training-camp-roster-2/|website=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2018|access-date=October 22, 2018}} ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2019–2024)=== On July 20, 2019, McLaughlin signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|title=TIMBERWOLVES SIGN JORDAN MCLAUGHLIN TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-sign-guard-jordan-mclaughlin-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 20, 2019|date=July 20, 2019}} On February 8, 2020, he recorded a career-high in points (24) and assists (11) against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401161424|title=McLaughlin, Beasley, new-look Wolves rout Clippers 142-115|work=ESPN.com|date=February 8, 2020|access-date=February 9, 2020}} On September 15, 2021, McLaughlin signed a standard contract with Minnesota.{{cite web|title=TIMBERWOLVES RE-SIGN JARRED VANDERBILT AND JORDAN MCLAUGHLIN|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-re-sign-jarred-vanderbilt-and-jordan-mclaughlin|website=NBA.com|date=September 15, 2021|access-date=September 16, 2021}} ===Sacramento Kings (2024–2025)=== On July 10, 2024, McLaughlin signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|title=Sacramento Kings Sign Jordan McLaughlin|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/sacramento-kings-sign-jordan-mclaughlin|website=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2024|access-date=July 10, 2024}} ===San Antonio Spurs (2025–present)=== On February 3, 2025, McLaughlin was traded, alongside [[De'Aaron Fox]], to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in a three-team trade also involving the [[Chicago Bulls]] in which [[Zach LaVine]], [[Sidy Cissoko]], three first-round picks and two second-round picks were sent to the Kings while [[Zach Collins]], [[Kevin Huerter]], [[Tre Jones]] and a 2025 first-round pick went to the Bulls.{{cite web|title=Spurs Acquire De'Aaron Fox and Jordan McLaughlin|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-acquire-deaaron-fox-and-jordan-mclaughlin|website=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2025|access-date=February 3, 2025}} On July 12, 2025, McLaughlin re-signed with the Spurs on a one-year, $3 million contract.{{cite web | last=Moreno | first=Amanda | title=San Antonio Spurs re-sign veteran guard Jordan McLaughlin | website=WOAI | date=2025-07-12 | url=https://news4sanantonio.com/news/local/san-antonio-spurs-re-sign-veteran-guard-jordan-mclaughlin-basketball-nba-local | access-date=2025-12-06}} ==Career
